title: The 60-30-10 Color Composition Rule
rule_statement: Anchor the outfit in 60% dominant base neutral (e.g. suit, coat, or trousers+sweater), 30% secondary harmonic hue (shirt, jacket, or skirt), and 10% high-contrast accent (shoes, tie, scarf, or bag).
negative_constraint: Do not divide the outfit into three equal 33% blocks of intensely competing colors.
example: 60% Charcoal trousers and coat, 30% Light blue Oxford shirt, 10% Burgundy leather loafers.

title: Tonal Monochromatic Harmony
rule_statement: When styling a single color family (e.g. all navy or all cream), vary the shades, values, and textures significantly across pieces to create depth and avoid a flat uniform appearance.
negative_constraint: Avoid pairing identical shades of the exact same flat cotton fabric unless it is a tailored matched suit.
example: Midnight navy wool overcoat over slate blue merino knitwear and dark navy selvedge jeans.

title: Analogous Warm & Cool Harmonies
rule_statement: Combine 2 to 3 shades that sit adjacent on the 12-spoke color wheel (e.g. olive green + mustard camel + warm rust) for an organic, sophisticated sartorial flow.
negative_constraint: Avoid mixing high-chroma adjacent primaries that clash without a neutral bridge.
example: Olive field jacket over a camel cashmere crewneck and ecru chinos.

title: Complementary Contrast Balancing
rule_statement: When pairing direct color-wheel opposites (e.g. navy blue with cognac orange, or forest green with deep burgundy), let one hue occupy 70-80% of the visual space while the other acts as an intentional accent.
negative_constraint: Do not balance two complementary colors in equal 50/50 visual weight.
example: Deep navy suit complemented by rich cognac leather shoes, cognac belt, and amber pocket square.

title: Neutral Anchor Stabilization
rule_statement: Ground vivid, saturated, or heavily patterned garments with classic neutral anchors (Charcoal, Black, White, Navy, Camel, Ecru, or Grey).
negative_constraint: Avoid pairing two clashing bold patterns on both top and bottom simultaneously.
example: A statement houndstooth or bright cobalt blazer anchored by clean black tailored trousers and crisp white top.

title: Tactile Texture Contrast
rule_statement: Balance fabric surfaces by pairing matte/rough textures with smooth/sheen textures (e.g. chunky cable-knit with smooth poplin, or brushed suede with raw denim).
negative_constraint: Do not combine all-flat, slick synthetic surfaces together in an outfit.
example: Coarse wool tweed blazer paired with a smooth silk-blend shirt and brushed cotton chinos.

title: Visual Fabric Weight Matching
rule_statement: Ensure the physical and visual weight of garments harmonizes: heavy fabrics (shearling, heavyweight wool, denim) require substantial footwear (boots, brogues, lug soles), not flimsy canvas shoes.
negative_constraint: Do not pair heavy winter outerwear with ultra-thin summery slip-on shoes or sandals.
example: Heavy wool double-breasted coat paired with sturdy Goodyear-welted leather Chelsea boots.

title: Daytime Sheen Balancing
rule_statement: Reserve high-sheen fabrics (satin, velvet, patent leather, sequins) for evening formalwear or restrained daytime accessory accents. Daytime looks must prioritize matte and natural finishes.
negative_constraint: Avoid patent leather shoes or high-gloss satin dresses in casual daytime or office settings.
example: Matte finish leather loafers for the office rather than high-gloss patent leather.

title: The 1:2 Golden Ratio (Rule of Thirds)
rule_statement: Construct the silhouette in 1/3 and 2/3 visual proportions (e.g. tucked-in top with high-waisted bottoms, or cropped jacket over a long dress) to elongate vertical proportions.
negative_constraint: Avoid bisecting the body exactly at the 50/50 midline with a long untucked boxy shirt ending mid-hip over untapered straight pants.
example: High-waisted tailored trousers (2/3 of silhouette) paired with a French-tucked blouse (1/3).

title: Volume Counterbalance Axiom
rule_statement: Balance volume across horizontal planes: if the top is voluminous, oversized, or chunky, keep the bottom structured or slim. If the bottom is wide-leg or pleated, keep the top fitted or defined.
negative_constraint: Avoid shapeless oversized top paired with oversized baggy bottoms unless deliberately styling an avant-garde runway silhouette with waist cinch.
example: An oversized boyfriend cashmere knit sweater balanced with straight-leg dark wash jeans and sleek ankle boots.

title: Sub-Zero Thermal Layering Hierarchy
rule_statement: When temperature is 5°C or below, enforce a three-layer thermal sandwich: breathable base layer (cotton/modal) -> insulating mid-layer (wool/cashmere/fleece) -> protective outer shell (wool coat or down puffer) with closed weather-sealed footwear.
negative_constraint: Strictly prohibit open-toe shoes, lightweight linen, bare ankles, or unlined lightweight jackets in freezing temperatures.
example: Thermal base top + merino wool turtleneck + heavy wool overcoat + lined leather boots.

title: Transitional Mid-Temperature Layering (6°C - 16°C)
rule_statement: In temperate to cool weather (6°C - 16°C), design flexible layered looks featuring a collared shirt or fine-gauge knit under a trench coat, blazer, or utility jacket that can be adjusted through the day.
negative_constraint: Avoid heavy sub-zero thermal puffers or lightweight summer shorts in 10-15°C climates.
example: Cotton Oxford shirt under a V-neck merino pullover and a classic cotton gabardine trench coat.

title: High-Heat Breathability (>25°C)
rule_statement: When temperature exceeds 25°C, prioritize natural, open-weave, moisture-wicking fabrics (linen, seersucker, lightweight cotton, silk) with relaxed breathable cuts and light reflective palettes.
negative_constraint: Strictly prohibit heavy wool, synthetic leather jackets, chunky fleece, or lined heavy boots in high summer heat.
example: Pure linen button-down shirt paired with tailored linen-cotton blend shorts or lightweight chinos and suede espadrilles.

title: Wet Weather & Precipitation Footwear Defense
rule_statement: In rain or wet conditions, select water-resistant treated leather or rubber footwear and darker bottom garments. Outerwear must feature water-repellent or dense wool protection.
negative_constraint: Strictly prohibit raw untreated suede shoes, pale white trousers, or delicate silk bottoms in rainy conditions.
example: Dark charcoal trousers with waterproof leather Chelsea boots and a water-resistant trench coat.

title: Business Formal Sartorial Standards
rule_statement: For business formal engagements, curate matching tailored dark two-piece suits (Navy or Charcoal), crisp white or pale blue collared dress shirts, silk neckwear, and polished leather Oxford or Derby shoes.
negative_constraint: Prohibit denim, t-shirts, athletic sneakers, casual knitwear without blazers, or novelty accessories.
example: Navy tailored suit, white poplin spread-collar shirt, navy polka dot silk tie, and black calfskin oxfords.

title: Smart Casual Sophistication
rule_statement: Blend formal structure with casual ease: pair a tailored blazer or fine knit with clean dark-wash denim or chinos, anchored by clean minimalist leather sneakers or loafers.
negative_constraint: Avoid distressed ripped jeans, athletic graphic hoodies, or formal tuxedo eveningwear in smart casual contexts.
example: Navy unconstructed hopsack blazer over a white crewneck tee, khaki chinos, and clean white leather dress sneakers.

title: Conservative & Religious Modesty Standards
rule_statement: For users with conservative or orthodox modesty preferences, ensure full coverage past elbows and below knees. Sleeveless, slip, or lower-neckline garments are permissible ONLY WHEN layered under an opaque blazer, cardigan, or jacket.
negative_constraint: Strictly prohibit unlayered sleeveless tops, mini skirts, sheer textiles, or exposed midriffs.
example: A sleeveless midi dress layered under a tailored wool-blend blazer and styled with closed-toe flats.

title: Ceremonial Color Etiquette
rule_statement: Observe cultural venue and ceremony norms: in Western weddings, avoid solid white dresses/gowns (reserved for the bride); in formal joyous occasions, balance solemn darks with uplifting harmonic color accents.
negative_constraint: Do not recommend a solid white lace dress to a guest attending a wedding. Strictly forbid beach flip-flops, casual slides, sweatpants, shorts, cargo pants with utility pockets, casual bomber jackets, graphic prints, and heavy combat/work boots for wedding guests. When the closet lacks formal attire, degrade to semi-formal or smart-casual and suggest missing formal pieces in shopping suggestions.
example: Emerald green or dusty rose midi cocktail dress with metallic neutral accessories for a wedding guest.

title: Mourning, Shiva & Funeral Etiquette (שבעה והלוויה)
rule_statement: For mourning visits, Shiva (שבעה), and funerals, wear modest, understated, solemn dark or muted neutral solid clothing (black, charcoal, dark grey, navy, dark brown, or subdued earth tones). Men: clean long trousers or dark solid jeans, with an unadorned solid collared shirt or neat solid tee. Women: modest unadorned tops with sleeves, long pants or below-knee skirts.
negative_constraint: Strictly prohibit graphic t-shirts, loud logos, eagle or animal prints, slogan tees, shorts, gym and athletic wear, beachwear, vibrant loud colors (red, yellow, orange, neon), distressed or ripped clothing, and comedy or party elements. In Hebrew, use 'לביקור שבעה' or 'לניחום אבלים', never 'להולך בישיבה שבעה'.
example: Charcoal tailored trousers or clean dark jeans paired with a plain black or navy polo/button-down shirt and dark subdued shoes.

title: Orthodox Jewish Modesty (צניעות - Tzniut)
rule_statement: For Orthodox Jewish modesty guidelines, women require skirts or dresses extending below the knee even when seated, sleeves extending past the elbow, and high necklines covering the collarbone with opaque fabrics. Men wear long trousers with collared shirts.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid trousers, shorts, or jeans for orthodox women. Forbid sleeveless tops, sheer fabrics, deep V-necks, low backs, or high leg slits.
example: Navy A-line pleated midi skirt falling well below the knee, paired with a long-sleeved silk-blend blouse with high jewel neckline.

title: Shabbat & Jewish Festive Attire (שבת וחגים)
rule_statement: For Shabbat meals, synagogue services, and Jewish holidays (Yom Tov), wear elevated, celebratory, elegant attire. Men wear crisp white or pastel button-down shirts, tailored trousers, blazers, and polished dress shoes. Women wear festive elegant midi or maxi dresses.
negative_constraint: Avoid casual workwear, gym clothes, distressed denim, graphic tees, or worn sneakers.
example: Crisp white tailored button-down shirt paired with charcoal dress trousers, navy hopsack blazer, and polished leather dress shoes.

title: Islamic Friday Prayer & Mosque Etiquette (صلاة الجمعة وزيارة المسجد)
rule_statement: For Jumu'ah Friday prayers, mosque visits, and sacred spaces, attire must be loose-fitting, clean, and fully modest. Men must cover from navel to below knee (long trousers or clean thobe). Women require loose abayas or maxi garments covering to wrists and ankles with a hijab.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid short-sleeve tops or shorts for all genders (arms and legs must be covered). Forbid animal prints (leopard, zebra, etc.), graphic/slogan tees, distressed/ripped clothing, sheer fabrics, or sleeveless/crop tops.
example: Clean tailored linen thobe or loose navy trousers with a pressed long-sleeved white tunic shirt and clean dress socks.

title: Hindu Funeral & Bereavement Etiquette (Antyeshti - अंतिम संस्कार)
rule_statement: For Hindu funerals, cremations, and mourning rites, wear plain, solid, unadorned white attire (white cotton kurta-pyjama or simple white cotton saree). White represents purity, detachment, and peaceful passage.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID BLACK CLOTHING: Black is considered highly inauspicious at Hindu funerals. Forbid vibrant colors (red, gold, bright yellow, hot pink). Forbid leather shoes or leather belts inside sacred cremation rituals.
example: Plain unembellished white cotton kurta paired with white cotton pyjama pants and simple non-leather slip-on shoes.

title: Hindu Wedding & Festival Celebrations (Vivaha & Diwali - विवाह उत्सव)
rule_statement: For Hindu weddings (Vivaha, Sangeet, Baraat) and festivals like Diwali, wear vibrant, auspicious, opulent celebratory colors (crimson red, deep maroon, gold, saffron, emerald green, royal navy, royal magenta) in traditional silk, brocade, or fine embroidery.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID SOLID BLACK: Black is considered inauspicious at Hindu wedding rituals. STRICTLY FORBID PLAIN UNADORNED WHITE: Plain white is reserved for bereavement and is avoided by wedding guests. STRICTLY FORBID CASUAL WEAR: Flip-flops, beach slides, casual slides, sweatpants, shorts, cargo pants with utility pockets, casual bomber jackets, graphic shirts/tees, and heavy combat/work boots are strictly inappropriate for a Hindu wedding. If the user's closet lacks traditional ethnic wear (Kurta, Churidar, Sherwani), suggest purchasing them in Stylist Recommendations (shopping suggestions) and gracefully curate the most respectful formal or semi-formal alternative (suit, blazer, tailored trousers, collared shirt, leather loafers).
example: Rich maroon or royal navy silk Kurta with an embroidered gold Nehru jacket and tailored churidar pants.

title: East Asian Funeral & Memorial Etiquette (葬礼 / お葬式 / 장례식)
rule_statement: For Chinese, Japanese, and Korean funerals and memorial services, wear plain, solemn, dark clothing—a tailored black suit with white dress shirt and solid plain black necktie for men; plain black formal dress or dark modest suit for women.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID RED AND GOLD: Red and gold are symbols of supreme celebration and are considered an extreme taboo and grave insult at East Asian funerals. Avoid colorful accessories, shiny jewelry, or flashy patterns.
example: Tailored solid black two-piece suit with a crisp white spread-collar dress shirt, matte solid black necktie, and polished black Oxford shoes.

title: East Asian Wedding Guest Etiquette (婚礼 / 結婚式)
rule_statement: For guests attending Chinese, Japanese, or Korean weddings and banquets, wear elegant, festive, respectful attire such as pastel, navy, grey, blush, or jewel-toned cocktail dresses or dark tailored suits with a celebratory tie.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID SOLID RED: At Chinese weddings, red is reserved exclusively for the bride. STRICTLY FORBID SOLID WHITE: Solid white is reserved exclusively for the bridal gown in modern ceremonies. Avoid mourning black suits paired with plain black ties.
example: Soft dusty-rose or navy cocktail dress, or a charcoal tailored suit with a champagne silk tie and pocket square.

title: Western Black Tie & Gala Protocol
rule_statement: For Black Tie galas, formal charity balls, and evening opera receptions, men strictly wear a black or midnight blue tuxedo with satin lapels, white pleated/pique tuxedo shirt, black silk bow tie, and patent leather dress shoes. Women wear floor-length evening gowns.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid daytime business suits, sports jackets, neckties (long ties), button-down collar shirts, chinos, loafers, or sneakers.
example: Midnight-blue shawl-collar tuxedo with black grosgrain lapels, crisp white pique wing-collar shirt, black silk grosgrain bow tie, and black patent dress shoes.

title: Christian Church, Cathedral & Holy Sanctuary Etiquette (כנסייה, מיסה ואתרים קדושים)
rule_statement: For Christian church services, Sunday Mass, cathedral visits, and pilgrimage to Holy Land sanctuaries (e.g. Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Vatican), wear dignified, respectful, modest attire. Shoulders, chest, and knees must be fully covered. Men wear smart collared shirts (button-down, neat polo, or fine knit), tailored trousers or dark chinos, and closed-toe dress shoes or clean loafers. Women wear modest dresses or skirts covering the knees, or elegant tailored slacks with covered shoulders.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid graphic tees, loud slogan prints, cartoon graphics, animal face prints, eagle prints, ripped or distressed denim, sleeveless tops, tank tops, crop tops, shorts, beachwear, flip-flops, or hats/caps inside the sanctuary.
example: Crisp pressed white or light blue Oxford button-down shirt paired with tailored charcoal trousers, navy blazer, and polished dark brown leather loafers.

title: Vatican & Papal Audience Protocol (Privilège du Blanc & Il Protocollo)
rule_statement: For papal audiences and Vatican Apostolic Palace engagements, attire must be conservative and formal. Men wear a dark conservative suit (charcoal or navy) with subdued tie and black leather dress shoes. Women wear a long-sleeved black dress or skirt suit falling well below the knee, high neckline, and a black lace mantilla (veil).
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid white, ivory, or cream dresses for women (Privilège du blanc is strictly reserved for reigning Catholic monarchs). Strictly forbid sleeveless tops, bare shoulders, necklines below collarbone, hemlines above knee, open-toed sandals, athletic footwear, loud neon colors, or caps/beanies.
example: Modest long-sleeved black crepe midi dress with high jewel neckline, black tailored wool blazer, black lace mantilla, and closed-toe black pumps.

title: Eastern Orthodox & Coptic Sanctuary Etiquette (Ορθόδοξη Εκκλησία / الكنيسة القبطية)
rule_statement: For Eastern Orthodox and Coptic church services and monasteries, attire requires reverence and modesty. Men wear long trousers with collared shirts and must remove all hats upon entering. Women wear below-the-knee modest skirts or dresses with covered shoulders and chest, often with a headscarf/foulard. In Coptic Holy of Holies, shoes are removed.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid women from wearing pants or trousers in traditional Orthodox monasteries (skirts only). Strictly forbid shorts, sleeveless tops, plunging necklines, or graphic prints. Men are strictly forbidden from wearing caps or hats inside.
example: Long-sleeved dusty blue blouse with high collar, modest charcoal A-line pleated wool-blend midi skirt, silk hair scarf, and closed-toe leather boots.

title: Western White Tie & State Banquet Protocol (Cravate Blanche)
rule_statement: For White Tie state banquets, royal coronations, and Nobel ceremonies, men wear a black wool tailcoat cut short in front with dual swallowtails, matching trousers with double side braid, white piqué stiff wing-collar shirt, white piqué low-cut waistcoat, white piqué bow tie, and black patent court pumps or oxfords. Women wear formal floor-length ball gowns.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid standard tuxedos, black bow ties with tails (reserved for waitstaff), colored waistcoats, business suits, daytime neckties, sneakers, or short cocktail dresses.
example: Black wool tailcoat with silk grosgrain peak lapels, white piqué wing-collar shirt, white piqué low-cut waistcoat, matching white bow tie, double-striped black trousers, and patent oxford shoes.

title: Synagogue Worship & Prayer Etiquette (בית כנסת ותפילה)
rule_statement: Attire for synagogue services and Western Wall (Kotel) visitation must reflect sanctity (Kavod HaTzibbur). Men wear long tailored trousers or smart chinos, collared button-down shirt or blazer, closed shoes, and head covering (Kippah). Women wear modest dresses or skirts covering knees, with covered shoulders and elbows.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid shorts, sleeveless shirts, gym wear, graphic tees, distressed/ripped denim, beach flip-flops, or bare heads for men. Forbid short skirts, bare midriffs, or low-cut tops for women.
example: Light blue poplin button-down shirt with navy unstructured wool blazer, medium-grey tailored trousers, suede Kippah, and polished leather loafers.

title: Brit Milah, Simchat Bat & Family Simchas (ברית מילה ושמחות)
rule_statement: Attire for circumcisions (Brit Milah), baby namings, and family simchas is elevated, joyful, smart-formal or cocktail in celebratory palettes (pastels, sky blue, cream, sage, festive navy). Men wear crisp dress shirts, blazers, and dress slacks. Women wear celebratory modest midi dresses or elegant suits.
negative_constraint: Avoid somber mourning all-black suits and black neckties. Forbid casual athletic attire, denim, t-shirts, or workout sneakers.
example: Crisp white spread-collar dress shirt with lavender woven silk tie, light grey wool-linen sports jacket, dark navy trousers, and cognac leather Derby shoes.

title: Tisha B'Av & Yom Kippur Footwear Protocol (תשעה באב ויום כיפור - איסור נעילת הסנדל)
rule_statement: Halakha strictly prohibits wearing leather shoes on Yom Kippur and the fast of Tisha B'Av. Worshippers must wear non-leather footwear made exclusively of canvas, rubber, cotton, or synthetic materials. Yom Kippur attire is traditionally pure white; Tisha B'Av attire is somber, plain, subdued mourning dress.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID LEATHER FOOTWEAR: Shoes, boots, sandals, or clogs containing any real leather or suede are forbidden. Avoid flashy luxury accessories, gold jewelry, or ornate embellishments.
example: Clean unadorned white linen-cotton tunic with relaxed stone cotton trousers and plain white non-leather canvas slip-ons.

title: Hajj & Umrah Pilgrimage Etiquette (الإحرام ومناسك الحج والعمرة)
rule_statement: For men in the sacred state of Ihram, clothing consists strictly of two seamless, unhemmed, unstitched sheets of white cotton/terrycloth (Izar and Rida). Footwear must leave ankles and foot bridge exposed (simple sandals). Women wear loose-fitting modest clothing (abaya) covering the whole body except face and hands.
negative_constraint: For men in Ihram: STRICTLY FORBID STITCHED OR TAILORED GARMENTS (no underwear, trousers, shirts, jackets, or socks). Forbid any head covering (caps, ghutras). For women in Ihram: STRICTLY FORBID NIQAB (face veil) AND GLOVES (face and hands must remain uncovered).
example: Two seamless sheets of unstitched pure white combed cotton waffle-weave cloth secured with travel belt, paired with non-stitched rubber open-instep sandals.

title: Eid al-Fitr & Eid al-Adha Festive Splendor (عيد الفطر وعيد الأضحى المبارك)
rule_statement: Following prophetic tradition (Sunnah), Muslims wear their finest, cleanest, often newly purchased clothing for Eid prayers and family feasts. Men wear pristine white or jewel-toned Thobes, Kurtas, or tailored suits. Women wear celebratory embroidered Abayas, Kaftans, or modest festive dresses with coordinated luxury hijabs.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid worn-out, stained, distressed casualwear (ripped jeans, faded t-shirts, gym sneakers). Prohibit revealing cuts (mini hemlines, low necklines, sheer textiles).
example: Opulent emerald green silk-crepe Kaftan with gold Zari hand-embroidery along neckline, champagne chiffon-silk hijab, and metallic leather kitten heels.

title: Arabian Gulf Formal Protocol & Bisht (البشت والكندورة الخليجية)
rule_statement: Formal, diplomatic, and wedding attire for Gulf Arab men consists of a tailored floor-length white or dark wool Thobe/Kandura, Ghutra/Shemagh headscarf with black Agal, and a Bisht (flowing camel-hair or wool cloak trimmed with gold Zari embroidery). Women wear haute-couture tailored Abayas with matching Sheila.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid wearing a Bisht with sportswear, denim, casual t-shirts, or athletic footwear. Forbid ill-fitting, wrinkled, or soiled Thobes.
example: Pristine white superfine cotton bespoke Thobe, sheer black wool Bisht with Saudi royal gold Zari trim, crisp white Ghutra with Agal, and ostrich leather sandals.

title: Maghrebi Djellaba, Kaftan & Babouche Etiquette (الجلابة والقفطان المغربي)
rule_statement: North African ceremonial attire centers on the Djellaba (long loose hooded robe with full sleeves), Gandora tunic, or ceremonial women's Takchita/Kaftan with gold Mdamma belt. Men and women wear handcrafted leather Babouche/Belgha slippers.
negative_constraint: Avoid cheap synthetic knockoffs with plastic trims. Strictly forbid wearing dirty sneakers or worn rubber flip-flops with a ceremonial silk Djellaba.
example: Olive green fine-wool woven Djellaba with handcrafted silk Sfifa and Aakad buttons over a white Gandora, with hand-stitched yellow leather Belgha slippers.

title: Southeast Asian Batik & Baju Melayu Protocol (Batik & Baju Melayu Nusantara)
rule_statement: In Indonesia and Malaysia, authentic long-sleeved silk Batik shirts are officially recognized formal business and diplomatic attire substituting for Western suits. For religious occasions and weddings, men wear the Baju Melayu tunic and trousers with Songket Kain Samping wrap and Songkok cap. Women wear Baju Kurung or Kebaya with Tudung.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid short-sleeved casual Hawaiian tourist print shirts in place of formal long-sleeved silk Batik. Do not omit the Kain Samping from ceremonial Baju Melayu.
example: Long-sleeved handcrafted silk Batik shirt in deep indigo Parang motif, tailored black formal wool trousers, and polished black leather Derby dress shoes.

title: Hindu Temple Darshan & Non-Leather Sanctum Protocol (मंदिर दर्शन एवं पूजा)
rule_statement: Visiting a Hindu Mandir for Darshan and Puja requires modesty and ritual purity. Men wear traditional unstitched or loose cotton/silk garments: Kurta with Pyjama, Dhoti, or Kurta with formal trousers. Women wear Sarees, Salwar Kameez with Dupatta, or Anarkalis covering shoulders and knees. Shoes are removed outside at the Charan Paduka.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID ALL LEATHER ARTICLES: Belts, shoes, watch straps, wallets, or handbags made of real animal leather are strictly forbidden inside the temple sanctum (representing ritual impurity and Ahimsa). Strictly forbid shorts, mini skirts, low-cut tops, or bare shoulders.
example: Saffron-gold pure raw silk Kurta with Mandarin collar, off-white cotton-linen drawstring churidar trousers (no leather belt), cotton Angavastram stole, and fabric slip-ons removed outside.

title: South Indian Kerala Temple Attire (കേരള ക്ഷേത്ര വസ്ത്രധാരണം - Mundu & Veshti)
rule_statement: In traditional Kerala and South Indian temples, Hindu men must enter the inner courtyard bare-chested (removing shirts and outerwear) wearing a pristine white/cream Mundu (cotton sarong with gold Kasavu border) with a folded Melmundu stole. Women wear the cream-and-gold Kasavu Saree or two-piece Set Mundu.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid stitched shirts, t-shirts, trousers, jeans, or shorts for men inside orthodox Kerala temple courtyards. Forbid synthetic colors or Western casual attire.
example: Handwoven Kerala double-Mundu in off-white organic cotton with 3-inch pure gold Kasavu border, with folded matching Melmundu draped over shoulder.

title: Buddhist Temple Visitation & Monastic Respect (วัดวาอาราม / 佛寺礼仪)
rule_statement: When visiting Buddhist temples, stupas, and wats (e.g. Thailand, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Japan, Tibet), attire must be calm, modest, and respectful. Shoulders, upper arms, and knees must be fully covered (ankle-length bottoms preferred). Shoes and hats must be removed before entering shrine halls.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID CLOTHING RESEMBLING MONASTIC ROBES: Laypersons must NEVER wear solid saffron, golden-orange, ochre, or Tibetan maroon robes reserved for ordained monks (Bhikkhus). Strictly forbid sleeveless tank tops, shorts, mini skirts, sheer tops, or garments with disrespectful Buddha graphics.
example: Airy cream cotton-linen long-sleeved tunic shirt paired with wide-leg navy lightweight linen trousers reaching past ankles and slip-on canvas shoes.

title: Buddhist Lay Meditation & Precept Observance (ชุดขาวปฏิบัติธรรม / Upāsaka White)
rule_statement: When lay devotees attend temple on holy observance days (Uposatha, Vesak) or attend meditation retreats observing Eight Precepts, canonical attire is entirely pure solid white (Chut Khao). White signifies simplicity, mental purity, renunciation of vanity, and equality.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid bright, multicolored, saturated garments. Avoid jewelry, makeup, loud patterns, tight activewear leggings, or luxury branding.

tags: ชุดปฏิบัติธรรม

example: Plain unadorned white cotton loose button-front meditation tunic with loose white drawstring wide-leg cotton pants and simple white socks.

title: Sikh Gurdwara Etiquette & Head Covering (ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਮਰਯਾਦਾ)
rule_statement: Entering a Sikh Gurdwara requires humility, equality, and reverence. MANDATORY HEAD COVERING: Every person must cover their head entirely with a Rumāl (cloth scarf), Patka, Dastar (turban), or Chunni. Feet must be bare: shoes and socks are removed at Joda Ghar, and feet are washed before entering Darbar Sahib. Clothing must be loose and modest.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID HATS AND CAPS: Baseball caps, beanies, fedoras, or sunhats are strictly forbidden as head coverings inside a Gurdwara. Strictly forbid bare heads. Strictly forbid shorts, mini skirts, or bare shoulders. STRICTLY FORBID TOBACCO OR ALCOHOL ON PERSON.
example: Breathable sky-blue cotton Kurta tunic with loose white cotton Pyjama pants and a royal blue cotton Rumāl tied securely covering all hair.

title: Japanese Kimono & Yukata Protocol: Left-Over-Right Rule (着物の左前・右前)
rule_statement: When wearing Japanese traditional clothing (Kimono, Yukata, Haori), the wearer must ALWAYS wrap the left collar over the right collar (Hidari-mae). For formal events, women wear silk Houmongi or Tomesode with an authentic Obi sash and white split-toe Tabi socks with Zōri sandals.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID WRAPPING RIGHT COLLAR OVER LEFT COLLAR: Right-over-left wrapping (Migi-mae) is exclusively reserved for dressing corpses for Buddhist cremation funerals. Crossing right-over-left on living persons is an ominous death taboo. Forbid bare feet with formal Kimono (must wear white Tabi).
example: Sage-green silk Houmongi kimono wrapped left collar over right collar, tied with gold brocade Fukuro Obi, pristine white split-toe Tabi socks, and lacquer Zōri sandals.

title: Korean Hanbok Wedding Palette & Maternal Etiquette (혼주 한복 색상 규정)
rule_statement: The traditional Korean Hanbok features the Jeogori jacket and Chima skirt for women, and Baji with Jeogori for men. At Korean weddings, Confucian protocol dictates maternal colors: The Mother of the Bride strictly wears warm tones (pink, coral, peach, soft red); The Mother of the Groom strictly wears cool tones (sky blue, indigo, navy, jade green, cyan).
negative_constraint: Mothers must never swap maternal color codes (groom's mother wearing pink or bride's mother wearing blue causes confusion and disrespect). Guests must avoid wearing bridal white or neon colors.
example: Ivory silk Jeogori jacket with blue cuff embroidery tied with navy Otgoreum ribbon, over a sky-blue raw silk floor-length Chima skirt and traditional Kkotsin shoes.

title: Chinese Cultural Green Hat Taboo (戴绿帽子 - Dài Lǜ Màozi)
rule_statement: In Chinese society, headwear for men should feature neutral or dark styling tones (black, navy, grey, charcoal, brown, camel).
negative_constraint: STRICTLY PROHIBIT MEN FROM WEARING GREEN HATS OR CAPS: In Chinese culture, wearing a green hat (dài lǜ màozi / 戴绿帽子) signifies that a man's wife or partner has committed adultery. Styling a man with a green cap, green beanie, or green fedora is an extreme cultural insult and taboo.
example: Tailored charcoal grey cashmere mock-neck sweater, camel wool trench coat, dark selvedge denim, and classic midnight navy or black wool beanie (strictly non-green).

title: Yoruba Ceremonial Agbada, Gele & Aso Ebi (Àgbàdá, Gèlè àti Aṣọ Ẹbí)
rule_statement: For major Yoruba celebrations, weddings, and chieftaincy events, men wear the grand 3-piece Agbada (inner Buba tunic, Sokoto drawstring trousers, and flowing embroidered Agbada outer robe) crowned by an embroidered Fila cap. Women wear an opulent Buba, Iro wrap skirt, sculpted Gele head-tie, and Ipele shoulder sash conforming to host Aso Ebi colors.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid wearing an Agbada without the Fila cap (considered incomplete and disrespectful). Do not let Agbada sleeves drag on the floor. Avoid breaking the designated host Aso Ebi color palette.
example: Royal purple handwoven Aso Oke 3-piece Agbada with gold geometric embroidery, matching purple Fila Gobi cap angled to the side, and dark leather loafers.

title: Igbo Chieftaincy Isiagu & Coral Regalia (Ịsị Àgụ na Ọkpụ Àgụ)
rule_statement: The Isiagu (tunic featuring embroidered lion/leopard heads) is the sovereign formal garment for Igbo men, cut as a long tunic paired with solid black/dark trousers, an Okpu Agu knit cap or red chieftaincy cap, and authentic cylindrical coral neck beads (Ijele). Women wear George fabric wrappers, embroidered blouses, and tiered coral beads.
negative_constraint: Forbid wearing an Isiagu with patterned or clashing bottoms (trousers must be plain solid black or dark to anchor the lion print). Non-titled men should not wear the solid red chief's cap unless conferred. Avoid cheap plastic imitation beads.
example: Black heavy velvet Isiagu tunic with gold woven lion-head medallions, tailored solid black slacks, genuine cylindrical coral neck beads, and red/black Okpu Agu cap.

title: Ghanaian Ashanti / Akan Kente & Mourning Etiquette (Kente & Kobene)
rule_statement: Authentic handwoven Kente is sacred heraldry. Gold/Yellow denotes royalty; Blue represents peace; Green represents growth. For celebrations, men drape multi-yard Kente toga-style over the left shoulder (leaving right arm free). Women wear 3-piece tailored Kaba and Slit. At funerals, mourners wear Kobene (fiery vermilion red) or Kuntunkuni (dark brown/black indigo cloth), never joyous gold Kente.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID JOYOUS GOLD/MULTICOLORED KENTE AT FUNERALS. Strictly forbid draping male Kente toga over the right shoulder (must always rest over the left shoulder). Avoid machine-printed polyester knockoffs.
example: Master handwoven Akan royal Kente cloth featuring gold, emerald, and crimson threads wrapped over the left shoulder, with traditional Ahenema leather sandals.

title: Zulu & South African Heritage Etiquette (Isicholo & Shweshwe)
rule_statement: For traditional South African ceremonies (Zulu Umabo weddings and heritage gatherings), married Zulu women wear the Isicholo (wide flared woven hat dyed red/ochre) with beaded capes. Celebratory dresses crafted from authentic indigo printed Shweshwe cotton are standard across southern Africa.
negative_constraint: Unmarried women do not wear the Isicholo (reserved for married women). Prohibit casual denim, sportswear, or plain Western loungewear at traditional lobola or umabo ceremonies.
example: Indigo-blue geometric printed authentic Shweshwe A-line midi dress with tiered ruffle hem, crimson red flared woven Isicholo hat, and beaded Zulu collar necklace.

title: Formal Guayabera Protocol & Caribbean Black Tie (Guayabera de Gala)
rule_statement: In tropical Latin America and the Caribbean, the Guayabera de gala (formal long-sleeved Guayabera) is recognized as formalwear substituting for a suit or tuxedo. Must feature 100% fine linen, 4 front pockets, vertical alforza pleats front and back, side button vents, and a straight hem worn strictly UNTUCKED, paired with tailored dress trousers and leather dress loafers.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID TUCKING IN A GUAYABERA: Tucking a Guayabera into trousers destroys its vents and pleats and is a major fashion blunder. Forbid short-sleeved casual Guayaberas at formal evening weddings. Forbid sneakers, flip-flops, or jeans.
example: Long-sleeved crisp white 100% Irish linen Guayabera de gala with 4 pockets and hand-stitched alforzas worn untucked, with dark charcoal tropical wool trousers and cognac woven leather loafers.

title: Latin American Quinceañera & Catholic Milestone (Quince Años)
rule_statement: A Quinceañera begins with a Catholic Mass of Thanksgiving followed by a formal gala. Men wear tailored suits with ties. Female guests wear elegant formal cocktail dresses or festive midi/maxi dresses with covered shoulders for the church liturgy.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID OUTSHINING OR COPYING THE QUINCEAÑERA: Female guests must NEVER wear a voluminous ball gown, tiara, or the signature celebration color theme chosen by the celebrant. Strictly forbid solid white or ivory gowns. Maintain church modesty during the preliminary Mass.
example: Navy blue pleated chiffon A-line midi dress with jewel neckline, matching lightweight pashmina shawl for the church service, silver leather clutch, and suede block heels.

title: Sigd Holiday Attire (חג הסיגד - Beta Israel Ethiopian Jewish Tradition)
rule_statement: Dress in pristine, respectful solid white clothing (white Habesha Kemis with Netela shawl for women; white collared shirt with light/white trousers and Netela/Tallit for men) to honor the sacred renewal of the covenant and longing for Jerusalem.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid graphic t-shirts, loud logos, eagle/animal prints, slogan tees, black/dark mourning clothes, distressed denim, shorts, or casual beach sandals.
example: White linen collared shirt with tailored light trousers and white Netela shawl.

title: Inuit Sinck Tuck & Winter Drum Dancing Protocol
rule_statement: Wear authentic Arctic insulated winter garments (Atigi/Amauti hooded parkas, Kamiks sealskin/caribou boots, or Mother-Hubbard Silapaaq fabric parkas) suitable for freezing conditions and communal drum dancing.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid thin canvas sneakers, un-insulated jackets, bare ankles, or commercial polyester costume caricatures.
example: Down-insulated Atigi parka with fur ruff, warm wool trousers, and thermal Kamik boots.

title: Mimouna Festive Attire (מימונה - North African Sephardic Tradition)
rule_statement: Wear celebratory traditional festive attire (embroidered Kaftans, Jelabas, velvet vests with gold Zari braid, Tarboush caps, and leather Babouche slippers) in joyful vibrant colors (gold, emerald green, royal blue, white).
negative_constraint: Avoid somber funeral black, austere mourning tones, or drab athletic gym wear.
example: Embroidered white and gold festive Kaftan with gold-threaded vest and leather Babouche.

title: Lag BaOmer Bonfire & Spark Safety (ל"ג בעומר והילולת הרשב"י)
rule_statement: Wear 100% natural, flame-resistant breathable fabrics (heavy cotton, denim, canvas, wool) and sturdy closed-toe boots or shoes for outdoor bonfires and Meron festivities.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid meltable synthetic garments (polyester windbreakers, thin nylon shells, acrylic fleece) near active fires, and avoid open-toed sandals or high heels.
example: Heavy cotton button-down over sturdy denim jeans and leather work boots.

title: Tu B'Av White Vineyard Attire (ט"ו באב - חג האהבה והפיוס)
rule_statement: Wear light, elegant, pure plain white garments (white linen dresses, white cotton button-downs, light chinos) following the ancient egalitarian tradition of joyful vineyard gatherings.
negative_constraint: Avoid dark or somber black clothing, and avoid ostentatious luxury logos or gaudy designer branding.
example: Crisp white linen button-down shirt paired with off-white cotton chinos and clean loafers.

title: Songkran Water Festival & Public Decency Protocol (เทศกาลสงกรานต์)
rule_statement: Wear colorful floral tropical Songkran shirts (Sua Songkran) with lightweight, quick-drying cotton or technical shorts and secure non-slip water-resistant sandals.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid sheer or thin white fabrics that become transparent when wet, strictly forbid shirtless men or bikini tops in public (criminal decency violation), and avoid dry-clean-only silk.
example: Vibrant floral print short-sleeved cotton shirt with quick-dry shorts and non-slip sandals.

title: Nowruz Spring Equinox Attire (نوروز - Nou-Poosh New Clothes)
rule_statement: Wear brand new, pristine, unworn clothes (Nou-poosh) in vibrant spring tones (emerald green, turquoise, rose, pastel yellow, crisp white) to welcome renewal and good fortune.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid old, worn-out, torn, or stained clothing, and avoid dreary funeral black or somber mourning apparel.
example: New crisp pastel green linen blazer with fresh white shirt and light beige chinos.

title: Korean Chuseok & Seollal Heritage Attire (추석 / 설날 - Chuseok-Bim & Seol-Bim)
rule_statement: Wear traditional Hanbok or dignified conservative smart-casual attire suitable for ancestral Charye rites and formal bowing to elders (Sebae).
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid distressed/ripped denim, tight mini skirts, shorts, sleeveless tops, or casual loungewear during ancestral rites.
example: Traditional silk Hanbok with Norigae ornament or navy tailored suit with clean collared shirt.

title: Holi Festival of Colors Attire (होली - Rangwali Holi)
rule_statement: Wear inexpensive, plain white or light cotton clothing (Kurta-pyjama or simple tee and trousers) specifically intended to be permanently colored with herbal powders (Gulal), with long sleeves to shield skin.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid expensive silk, wool, cashmere, dry-clean-only garments, leather footwear, or items you intend to wear again.
example: Plain white cotton kurta-pyjama with sunglasses and washable canvas footwear.

title: Bavarian Oktoberfest Trachten & Dirndl Bow Protocol
rule_statement: Men wear authentic leather Lederhosen with H-suspenders, Trachten shirt, and Haferlschuhe; women wear a classic knee-length or midi Dirndl with bodice, blouse, and apron with bow placed according to relationship status.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid cheap shiny polyester mini-dirndls ('Halloween costumes'), plastic Lederhosen, fluorescent neon colors, or athletic sneakers.
example: Midi linen Dirndl with cotton apron bow tied on the right or left, paired with classic Haferlschuhe.

title: Intertribal Powwow & Ribbonwork Protocol
rule_statement: Wear below-the-knee ribbon skirts or tailored ribbon shirts with moccasins or neat clean footwear, respecting sacred tribal regalia.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid non-indigenous guests from wearing eagle feathers, warbonnets, or sacred ceremonial regalia; forbid short skirts above the knee, crop tops, or alcohol.
example: Dark cotton ribbon skirt adorned with satin prayer ribbons, paired with modest black blouse and soft moccasins.

title: Mexican Día de los Muertos Attire (Día de Muertos)
rule_statement: Wear celebratory traditional Mexican attire (embroidered Puebla dresses, elegant Catrina lace gowns, Charro suits) accented with vibrant marigold floral crowns and artistic sugar skull face art.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid gory horror movie masks, fake blood, gruesome props, or mocking cultural caricatures.
example: Black lace Catrina dress with vibrant marigold floral headpiece and embroidered shawl.

title: Ethiopian Orthodox Timkat & Meskel Attire (ጥምቀት እና መስቀል)
rule_statement: Wear pristine white handwoven Habesha Kemis and white cotton Netela or Gabi shawls with woven Tibeb borders, paired with comfortable flat footwear for outdoor processions.
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid black or dark funeral mourning clothes, shorts, sleeveless shirts, or revealing cuts.
example: White woven cotton Habesha dress with colorful Tibeb hem, draped with a white Netela shawl.

title: Scottish Burns Night & Highland Dress Protocol
rule_statement: Men wear authentic Highland dress (Prince Charlie or Argyll jacket, 8-yard clan tartan kilt, sporran, kilt hose, flashes, sgian-dubh, ghillie brogues, bow tie); women wear evening dress with clan tartan sash.
negative_constraint: Avoid wearing the sporran off-center, avoid mixing mismatched clan tartans, and forbid casual denim, trainers, or non-traditional novelty kilts.
example: Prince Charlie black wool jacket with clan tartan kilt, leather sporran, and ghillie brogues.

title: Egyptian & Levantine Galabiya Protocol (الجلابية المصرية والشامية)
rule_statement: The Galabiya / Jalabiya is a traditional full-length flowing robe worn in Egypt, Sudan, and the Levant. For daytime and casual social gatherings, choose breathable natural linen or Egyptian cotton in neutral or earth tones. For festive, ceremonial, or guest occasions, choose formal Galabiyas featuring tailored embroidery along the collar, placket, and cuffs (Tawshih). Pair strictly with traditional leather slip-on sandals or handmade babouche slippers.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID pairing a Galabiya with athletic sneakers, running shoes, baseball caps, or heavy combat boots. Never attempt to tuck a Galabiya into pants or wear a belt over traditional loose-cut Galabiyas.
example: Crisp sand-beige Egyptian linen Galabiya with subtle tone-on-tone embroidery on the neckline, paired with brown woven leather sandals.

title: Contemporary & Traditional Abaya Layering Protocol (العباية والشيلة)
rule_statement: The Abaya is an elegant modest garment worn across the Arabian Peninsula, Levant, and global Islamic communities. Closed Abayas function as the core Full Body garment. Front-open kimono-style Abayas function as an Outerwear duster coat layered over an opaque modest inner maxi dress, slip, or tailored wide-leg trousers. Always coordinate with a matching or harmonic Sheila / Hijab and elegant pointed flats, minimalist block heels, or refined mules.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID translucent or sheer inner garments beneath an open Abaya. Forbid pairing open Abayas with shorts, mini skirts, distressed denim, or plunge necklines. Avoid neon clashing colors for traditional conservative formal events.
example: Textured charcoal linen front-open Abaya layered over a cream satin-crepe inner column dress, styled with a matching charcoal chiffon Sheila and pointed leather mules.

title: Arabian Thobe, Kandura & Dishdasha Sartorial Etiquette (الثوب والكندورة)
rule_statement: The Thobe (also known as Kandura or Dishdasha) is the foundational traditional men's garment across the Arab world. For warm weather and daytime formal events, wear a crisp, impeccably pressed white, off-white, or cream cotton Thobe. For winter and cool climates, wear heavyweight wool or cashmere-blend Thobes in rich muted tones (navy, charcoal, camel, forest green). Pair with a crisp white Ghutra or red-and-white houndstooth Shemagh held with an Agal, and luxury leather sandals (Na'al) or tailored Oxford dress shoes.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID wearing a wrinkled, stained, or ill-fitting Thobe. Forbid pairing formal Thobes with athletic sneakers, flip-flops, denim jackets, or casual baseball caps.
example: Tailored Japanese cotton white Thobe with French cuffs, paired with a red-and-white houndstooth Shemagh, double-black cord Agal, and handcrafted calfskin leather sandals.

title: South Asian Kurta-Pyjama & Sherwani Formal Protocol (कुर्ता / शेरवानी)
rule_statement: In South Asian traditional menswear (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh), the Kurta functions as a versatile Top worn over Churidar (fitted tapered pants), Pyjama (loose straight trousers), or a Dhoti. For festivals and formal weddings, layer with an embroidered Nehru / Modi jacket or an ornate tailored Sherwani / Achkan (Outerwear coat) crafted from raw silk, brocade, or Jamdani. Complete the ensemble with handcrafted leather Mojari or Jutti footwear.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID wearing a Kurta with athletic running shoes, gym shorts, or ripped denim. Avoid pairing heavy winter brocade Sherwanis with ultra-casual flip-flops or plastic sandals.
example: Raw silk ivory Kurta with gold zari Mandarin collar, paired with fitted off-white Churidar pants, a royal sapphire embroidered velvet Nehru vest, and handcrafted leather Mojaris.

title: Traditional Saree Draping & Lehenga Choli Ensemble (साड़ी / लहंगा चोली)
rule_statement: Traditional South Asian festive and wedding attire for women centers on the Saree or Lehenga Choli. A Saree (6 to 9 yards of Banarasi, Kanjeevaram, or Chanderi silk) requires a tailored fitted Blouse (Choli) and an inskirt/petticoat, draped with structured pleats and a flowing shoulder pallu. A Lehenga Choli consists of an ornate flared maxi skirt (Lehenga), a fitted blouse (Choli), and a sheer or embroidered Dupatta scarf pinned securely across the shoulder/chest for modesty. Accessorize with traditional gold or Kundan jewelry and embellished sandals or juttis.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID wearing a Saree without a secure inskirt or proper blouse foundation. Forbid wearing western athletic sneakers, plastic flip-flops, or casual denim jackets over a formal Saree or Lehenga.
example: Crimson Banarasi silk Saree with gold woven floral motifs, paired with a matching elbow-sleeve brocade blouse, gold Kundan necklace, and gold metallic sandals.

title: Alan Flusser's Pattern Scale Hierarchy
rule_statement: Adjacent patterned garments must feature distinctly different physical scales (e.g. macro-scale windowpane jacket over micro-scale grid check shirt or pin-stripe). Ensure one pattern dominates while the secondary remains fine or dense.
negative_constraint: Never pair overlapping patterns of identical gauge, width, or millimeter spacing to prevent optical moire vibration.
example: Macro windowpane sports coat over micro gingham button-down and a solid grenadine silk tie.

title: Geometric vs Curvilinear Pattern Balancing
rule_statement: Balance rectilinear geometric patterns (stripes, checks, windowpanes) by pairing them with curvilinear or organic patterns (paisley, foulard, polka dots, florals) sharing a common base color.
negative_constraint: Do not stack identical geometric shapes (e.g. grid check shirt under grid check jacket) without contrasting shapes.
example: Fine stripe dress shirt paired with a neat geometric foulard or pin-dot silk necktie.

title: Munsell 12-Season Personal Color Flow
rule_statement: Coordinate garments based on the wearer's dominant personal color dimension: Hue (Warm vs Cool), Value (Light vs Deep), and Chroma (Bright/Clear vs Muted/Soft). Cool/Deep types thrive in sapphire and charcoal; Warm/Muted types thrive in olive, rust, and camel.
negative_constraint: Avoid placing stark high-contrast optic white or pitch black next to low-contrast warm/muted complexions; avoid muddy earth tones on high-chroma clear winters.
example: Deep Winter: Jet black overcoat with royal cobalt scarf. Soft Autumn: Olive field jacket with oatmeal knitwear.

title: Leather & Hardware Synchronization Protocol
rule_statement: Leather accessories (shoes, belt, watch strap, briefcase/bag) must reside within the same chromatic family (black with black; cognac/brown with matching brown). Visible metallic hardware (belt buckle, watch case, cufflinks, jewelry) must harmonize in color temperature (all silver/chrome or all gold/brass).
negative_constraint: Strictly forbid pairing black leather dress shoes with a brown leather belt, or clashing bright yellow-gold buckles with chrome steel watch cases.
example: Dark brown leather Chelsea boots, dark brown calfskin belt with brass buckle, and warm leather-strap gold watch.

title: Black Tie Waistband and Lapel Protocol
rule_statement: Formal black-tie dinner jackets mandate peak lapels or a shawl collar with matching grosgrain or satin facings, paired with trousers featuring a clean waistband (no belt loops, held by braces or side-tabs) and a single matching side braid.
negative_constraint: Never wear a standard leather belt or notch-lapel lounge suit jacket with a formal black-tie tuxedo.
example: Midnight blue dinner jacket with black silk grosgrain peak lapels, side-tab trousers with matching grosgrain stripe, white marcella bib shirt, black silk bow tie, and patent leather oxfords.

title: Tailoring Proportions: Collar Line & Bottom Button Axiom
rule_statement: On single-breasted two-button or three-button suit jackets and vests, leave the bottom button unfastened to preserve the garment's natural hip flare. Ensure the jacket collar hugs the shirt collar flush (no rear collar gap), showing exactly 1/4 to 1/2 inch of shirt cuff at the wrist.
negative_constraint: Never fasten the bottom button of a suit jacket, which creates severe pulling wrinkles ('X-crease') across the torso and distorts the drape.
example: Navy worsted two-button jacket fastened at top button only, revealing 1/2 inch of crisp white poplin cuff.

title: Aesthetic Sensuality: The Singular Exposure Axiom
rule_statement: Elevated sensual styling preserves erotic curiosity and refinement by exposing only ONE anatomical zone at a time (décolletage OR legs OR open back). Pair body-skimming silhouettes in high-tactile natural fabrics (mulberry silk, fine cashmere, glove leather) rather than compressive tightness.
negative_constraint: Avoid simultaneously revealing a plunging neckline, high mini-hemline, and bare back, which destroys aesthetic tension and projects visual desperation.
example: A high-neck, long-sleeved silk midi dress with a dramatic deep back cut, paired with sleek pointed pumps.

title: Executive Presence: Warmth vs Competence Balance
rule_statement: In high-stakes corporate leadership, client pitches, and negotiations, project unassailable competence and trustworthy warmth simultaneously by selecting Deep Navy or Charcoal worsted wool tailoring over stark pitch black, softened with fine-gauge knitwear or poplin.
negative_constraint: Avoid head-to-toe stark black tailoring in collaborative daytime business settings, which triggers subconscious social and referee penalties for aggression and unapproachability (Frank & Gilovich, 1988).
example: Tailored midnight navy blazer over an ivory merino wool crewneck and charcoal trousers.

title: Enclothed Cognition: Architectural Tailoring for Focus
rule_statement: Structured tailoring (defined shoulder lines, peaked lapels, clean unbroken vertical columns) increases felt power and abstract cognitive processing (Slepian et al., 2015), priming executive presence, decisive thinking, and high-level focus.
negative_constraint: Avoid wearing loose, shapeless, or overly slouchy garments during critical negotiations, interviews, or strategic executive presentations.
example: Single-breasted charcoal blazer with structured roped shoulders, paired with an unbroken column of matching trousers.

title: The Universal Capsule Foundation: High Combinatorial Density
rule_statement: Ground the wardrobe in high-GSM, seasonless neutral essentials (Oxford button-downs, raw selvedge denim, deconstructed navy wool blazer, tailored trousers, cashmere knits) that cross-pair seamlessly between casual, smart-casual, and business formal.
negative_constraint: Avoid accumulating hyper-specific single-use fast-trend garments that cannot be styled into at least three distinct multi-tier outfits.
example: A single deconstructed navy blazer worn formally with grey wool trousers and tie, or dressed down with white tee and raw denim.

title: Pediatric Health & Sensory Textile Safety (AAP / CPSC)
rule_statement: Children's and infants' apparel must prioritize breathable, hypoallergenic 100% GOTS-certified organic cotton or bamboo, tagless flat-locked seams, reinforced double knees, and elasticized waistbands to protect thin skin, prevent atopic dermatitis, and foster fine-motor dressing autonomy (AOTA). Sleepwear must be snug-fit without toxic chemical flame retardants.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID drawstrings or cords on children's hoods, necks, or waists (CPSC strangulation hazard); avoid scratchy synthetic polyester or unlined wool directly against child skin.
example: Tagless organic cotton zip romper with chin zipper guard, or reinforced-knee cotton joggers with elastic waistband.

title: The Red Sneakers Effect: Strategic Creative Nonconformity
rule_statement: In creative agencies, tech executive suites, and innovative industries, a deliberate signal of nonconformity (e.g. minimalist luxury sneakers with an architectural tailored suit) communicates high autonomy, status, and competence (Bellezza, Gino & Keinan, Harvard/JCR).
negative_constraint: Nonconformity must be intentional and pristine; accidental dress code violations, sloppy tailoring, or scuffed footwear signal carelessness rather than elevated status.
example: Architectural charcoal wool tailored suit paired with clean, minimalist white leather luxury sneakers.

title: Kaftan vs. Kurta: Origin, Silhouette, Construction & Pairing Protocol (قفطان مقابل كورتا / כפתן מול קורטה / काफ्तान बनाम कुर्ता)
rule_statement: Distinguish Kaftans and Kurtas by origin, construction, length, and pairing: (1) ORIGIN: The Kaftan (Caftan) originates in ancient Mesopotamia, Persia, and the Middle East (from Turkic 'kap ton' meaning 'covering garment'), spreading through the Ottoman Empire, Morocco/North Africa (Takchita), and West Africa (Senegalese/Nigerian kaftans). The Kurta is indigenous to South Asia (India and Pakistan). (2) SILHOUETTE & CONSTRUCTION: A Kaftan is a wide, loose, flowing single-piece garment cut broadly from shoulder to hem with NO defined shoulder seams or waist seams, characterized by wide 'batwing' or kimono-style sleeves and an unstructured or drawstring-cinched drape. A Kurta is a more tailored, structured tunic with defined shoulder seams, set-in sleeves, structured necklines (Mandarin/Nehru stand collar, keyhole, or button placket), and side slits ('chaak') from hip to hem for ease of movement. (3) LENGTH & PAIRING: Kaftans range from knee-length to floor-length and are worn standalone as a dress, resort cover-up, or formal evening gown. Kurtas fall to the knees or mid-calf and are almost always paired with bottoms (palazzos, churidars, salwars, straight cigarette pants, skirts, or dhoti pants) and often a dupatta.
negative_constraint: Never classify a structured shoulder-seamed South Asian Kurta with side slits as a Kaftan, nor classify a wide batwing-sleeved seamless Kaftan as a standard tailored Kurta. Do not leave a traditional knee-length Kurta unpaired without bottoms.
example: Standalone floor-length emerald silk Moroccan Kaftan with wide batwing sleeves and gold belt for resort/evening galas; or a tailored mustard-yellow Jaipur cotton Kurta with defined shoulders, side slits, paired with an ivory pleated skirt or palazzo pants for festive daytime wear.

title: The Hybrid Kaftan Kurta, Body-Type Fit & Festive Endurance Protocol (काफ्तान कुर्ता सेट / כפתן-קורטה)
rule_statement: The Kaftan Kurta (and Suit Kaftan / Kaftan Kurta Set) is a modern Indo-Western fusion garment merging the wide, airy batwing sleeves and relaxed shoulder-to-hem drape of a Kaftan with the traditional neckline (V-neck, Mandarin/Nehru collar, or embroidered placket), calf/knee length, and bottom pairing (straight pants, palazzos, or tulip pants) of a South Asian Kurta. (1) BODY-TYPE GUIDANCE: Kaftan silhouettes and V-neck/empire-waist Kaftan Kurtas excel on Apple, Strawberry (inverted triangle), Pear, and Maternity body types because the unconstructed batwing drape skims the midsection without clinging; Hourglass and Petite frames benefit from a drawstring, belted waist, or tailored straight/A-line Kurta to prevent fabric overwhelm. (2) FESTIVE ENDURANCE & OCCASION: Choose Kaftan or Kaftan Kurta sets in breathable linen (55–60 Lea), cotton cambric, modal satin, or georgette for warm, humid climates, daytime Haldi/Mehendi, travel, and floor-sitting Puja rituals (zero waist or armhole restriction). Choose structured Silk, Chanderi, or Brocade Kurta Sets (or Kashmiri Aari/Tilla embroidered Velvet Kaftan Kurtas) for formal stage receptions, office ethnic days, and structured ceremonies.
negative_constraint: Avoid stiff, heavy, high-neck, or boxy unshaped fabrics on apple-shaped or petite wearers in kaftan silhouettes, as they add visual bulk around the bust and shoulders. Avoid tight armhole or waist-pinching tailoring for long floor-sitting rituals in humid weather.
example: A V-neck hand-block printed mulmul cotton Kaftan Kurta with subtle waist drawstring, paired with tapered ivory cotton cigarette pants and juttis for a daytime festive brunch or Puja.

title: Kurta vs. Kurti & Nehru Collar Styling Protocol (कुर्ता बनाम कुर्ती / קורטה מול קורטי)
rule_statement: Differentiate traditional Kurtas from modern Kurtis by length, cut, and styling versatility: (1) KURTA: Traditional unisex or gender-specific South Asian garment extending to the knees, mid-calf, or ankles (including Straight-cut, A-line, Anarkali, and Angrakha silhouettes), crafted in cotton, silk, khadi, chanderi, or brocade and paired with churidars, salwars, palazzos, dhotis, or lehengas/skirts. (2) KURTI: A shorter, modernized feminine tunic originating in Northern India that falls at the waist, hips, or upper/mid-thigh, featuring contemporary sleeve and neckline variations (sleeveless, cold-shoulder, bell sleeves, asymmetrical hems, peplum, shirt-style, or Mandarin/Nehru collar) and styled effortlessly with jeans, jeggings, leggings, trousers, or dhoti pants for college, daily office, and Indo-Western casual wear. (3) NEHRU / MANDARIN COLLAR: A structured 1–1.5 inch stand-up collar with a split V-placket frames the collarbone cleanly for workwear, travel, and formal events without needing a dupatta or heavy necklace (pair with statement earrings or oxidized silver studs instead).
negative_constraint: Do not wear heavy chokers or bulky necklaces over a closed Nehru/Mandarin stand collar, as they clash with the structured neckline. Do not confuse a hip-length modern Kurti worn with denim jeans with a traditional calf-length ceremonial Kurta.
example: Indigo cotton Nehru-collar straight Kurta with 3/4 sleeves paired with white cigarette pants and oxidized silver jhumkas for smart office wear; or a hip-length printed cotton Kurti paired with blue denim jeans and kolhapuri flats for casual college outings.

negative_constraint: Never treat a standalone suit vest, casual graphic tee, or cargo pants as a substitute for a complete formal suit or tailored dress shirt. When recommending missing formal staples, always specify exact garment + cut/pieces + color + fabric + occasion.

rule_statement: Every versatile everyday wardrobe requires high-combinatorial core separates: (1) Heavyweight solid crewneck t-shirts in neutral anchors (optic white, black, heather grey) made of 100% combed cotton; (2) A smart-casual button-down shirt in light blue Oxford cloth or classic blue/brown plaid flannel; (3) A fine-gauge merino wool or cashmere crewneck/V-neck knit sweater in navy, charcoal, or camel for transitional layering; (4) Clean dark-indigo straight-leg selvedge denim jeans (unripped); and (5) Tailored beige, khaki, or olive cotton-twill chinos.

title: Essential Wardrobe Pillar 3: All-Weather Outerwear & Rain Protection Staples (פריטי בסיס להגנה ממזג אוויר ומעילים)
rule_statement: A functional four-season wardrobe must include dedicated outer-shell protection across temperature and precipitation extremes: (1) A waterproof breathable raincoat or classic water-repellent cotton-gabardine trench coat (in beige, olive, or navy) for rainy days; (2) An insulated tailored wool overcoat (charcoal, camel, or black) or thermal down parka for cold winter weather; and (3) A lightweight transitional jacket (denim jacket, suede bomber, or cotton field jacket) for mild autumn/spring layering.
negative_constraint: Indoor knit cardigans, hoodies, or unlined suit blazers cannot substitute for a waterproof raincoat or winter overcoat during precipitation and cold fronts.

title: Statutory Civilian Camouflage & Military Apparel Bans (איסור פלילי על לבוש צבאי והסוואה)
rule_statement: When traveling to the Caribbean (Barbados, Jamaica, Trinidad & Tobago, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent, Antigua & Barbuda, Grenada, Dominica, Saint Kitts & Nevis, Bahamas, Guyana), Africa (Nigeria, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Rwanda), or the Philippines, Oman, and Saudi Arabia, select solid earth-tone, khaki, olive, or linen resort and safari garments instead of any camouflage print.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID packing or wearing any camouflage-patterned clothing, shorts, hats, backpacks, Crocs/shoes, or children's items (even pink/blue fashion camo), which is a strict-liability criminal offense resulting in airport customs confiscation, fines, or military court-martial. In Uganda, also strictly forbid red berets (UPDF Act s. 160).
example: Solid sand-colored 100% linen trousers paired with a breathable white cotton shirt and a solid canvas backpack.

title: State-Mandated Religious Modesty & Public Decency Laws (חוקי צניעות ממלכתיים במזרח התיכון ואסיה)
rule_statement: In jurisdictions with statutory morality or public decency codes—Iran (Penal Code Art. 638 & 2024 Hijab Law), Afghanistan (2024 Virtue & Vice Law), Saudi Arabia (Public Decency Regulation), Brunei (Syariah Code s. 197/198), Aceh Indonesia (Qanun Jinayat), Maldives inhabited local islands, UAE (especially Sharjah), Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, and Malaysian government buildings—dress in loose, opaque garments covering shoulders to at least below the knees (and full headscarf + loose mid-thigh/knee manteau over ankle-length bottoms for women in Iran; full abaya/hijab in Afghanistan; full Chador inside Iranian shrines and black Iraqi Abaya inside Karbala/Najaf shrines).
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID men's or women's shorts in Iran, Afghanistan, Aceh, Chechnya, and Malaysian courts/ministries; forbid bikinis on inhabited Maldives islands outside fenced Bikini Beaches; forbid cross-dressing in Brunei, Kuwait, and Oman; forbid Western neckties in Afghan and Iranian state ministries.
example: Loose-fitting long-sleeved linen tunic (manteau) extending to the knees over wide-leg ankle-length trousers with a draped silk-cotton headscarf.

title: European & Quebec Secular Face-Covering & Public Laïcité Laws (איסור כיסוי פנים וחוקי חילוניות באירופה וקוויבק)
rule_statement: In France (Law 2010-1192), Switzerland (Federal Face-Covering Ban 2025), Austria (AGesVG), Belgium (Art. 563bis), Denmark (§ 134c), Bulgaria, the Netherlands (public transport, schools, hospitals, government buildings), and Quebec, Canada (Bill 21 public services), keep the face uncovered in public spaces. In French municipal swimming pools, men must wear fitted Lycra swim briefs rather than loose boardshorts, and women must wear standard one- or two-piece swimsuits rather than burkinis.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID full-face coverings (niqab, burqa, balaclavas, face-concealing masks) in public streets/transport across France, Switzerland, Austria, Belgium, Denmark, and Bulgaria (fines €150 to CHF 1,000); forbid abayas, qamis, and conspicuous religious symbols in French public schools.
example: Modest tailored trench coat over ankle-length trousers and a classic silk foulard worn around the hair and neck leaving the face completely uncovered.

title: Authoritarian State Dress Codes, Lèse-Majesté & Totalitarian Symbol Bans (חוקי לבוש ממלכתיים ואיסור סמלים פוליטיים)
rule_statement: Adhere strictly to national sartorial statutes: In North Korea (DPRK), wear formal tailored suits/dresses with closed shoes at Kumsusan Palace and Mansudae; in Bhutan (Driglam Namzha), wear long-sleeved collared shirts and ankle-length bottoms with no hats/umbrellas inside Dzongs; in Thailand, wear tailored trousers/long skirts (no sarongs over shorts) at the Grand Palace and respect Royal Lèse-Majesté (Art. 112) and Flag laws.
negative_constraint: STRICTLY FORBID blue/ripped/skinny jeans and leather trench coats in North Korea; forbid shorts in Ashgabat (Turkmenistan) and Grozny (Chechnya); forbid Thai flag prints on shoes/shorts or Buddha prints/lower-body tattoos in Thailand; forbid Nazi symbols in Germany/Austria (§ 86a), Soviet/Russian 'Z'/'V'/St. George ribbon symbols in Ukraine/Baltics/Poland, Communist hammer-and-sickle shirts in Indonesia (KUHP Art. 188), protest-slogan shirts in Hong Kong (NSL), and rainbow symbols in Russia.
example: Long-sleeved collared linen shirt buttoned to the neck, tailored full-length cotton chinos, and closed leather loafers.

title: Territorial Faction, Gang & Cartel Apparel Safety Protocol (כללי בטיחות לבוש באזורי סכנה וכנופיות)
rule_statement: When traveling in or near urban peripheral communities or conflict regions in Latin America, the Caribbean, or South Africa, wear neutral, unbranded, non-factional casual clothing in muted tones (white, grey, beige, navy) with plain footwear.
negative_constraint: In Brazilian favelas (Rio, Salvador, Fortaleza), STRICTLY FORBID Adidas three-stripe apparel (TCP/BDM 'Tudo 3' marker), solid red or Nike gear in rival zones (CV 'Tudo 2'), Mickey Mouse shirts, and Joker/clown prints/tattoos, and ALWAYS remove motorcycle helmets at favela entrances. In El Salvador, Honduras, and Guatemala, forbid numbers 13, 18, XIII, XVIII, Nike Cortez shoes, and visible gothic tattoos. In rural Colombia and Mexico, forbid camouflage, tactical chest bags (pecheras), rubber jungle boots, and cartel caps (JGL, 701, MZ, Chapiza, CJNG). In Kingston (Jamaica) garrisons, avoid solid green (JLP) vs. solid orange (PNP); in Belfast interface zones, avoid sectarian Celtic/Rangers jerseys.
example: Plain unbranded grey cotton crewneck T-shirt, beige chino trousers, and unbranded white leather sneakers.
